source.title: Phases of learning dynamics in artificial neural networks in the absence or presence of mislabeled data

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present
record.tranche_reason: The paper measures test-error dynamics during SGD training with randomly mislabeled examples, using a different setup from the listed versions.
record.gate_note: The paper cites prior work on fitting random labels but reports no experiment fitting a fully random-label dataset. Its own results concern clean training and training with mixtures of correctly and randomly mislabeled examples. Values shown only in figures are recorded as figure only.
record.test_reason: The study measures SGD dynamics with mixtures of natural and randomly corrupted labels and evaluates a cleaning procedure. It does not report the natural-label versus fully random-label comparison required by V1 or test any other listed version. Its discussion of random-label capacity and double descent relies on prior work.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors present a statistical-physics framework for distinguishing SGD learning phases, associate late fitting of corrupted labels with rising test error, and use phase-II loss separation to guide cleaning. They also report no significant difference between cleaning followed by continued training and early stopping in their experiments.
record.recipe_differences: Uses SGD on MNIST and CIFAR10 with randomly mislabeled samples and tracks learning dynamics and test error; it does not reproduce the random-label memorization comparison in the cited original work.
record.method_sensitivity: The final test error rises almost linearly with mislabeled fraction; minimum test error is roughly stable at small fractions, then rises sharply and approaches the final error when ρ > 0.85.

fits_no_version.finding: With mixed natural and corrupted labels, test error initially decreases, plateaus, then increases while training errors approach zero. Final test error increases nearly linearly with corruption fraction.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: During SGD training on corrupted labels, natural-label learning can precede memorization of corrupted examples, producing a U-shaped test-error trajectory.

fits_no_version.finding: Phase-II high-loss cleaning recovers more than half the accuracy difference between uncleaned and correctly labeled-only training for noise levels up to 80%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Removing high-loss examples during maximum loss-distribution separation can improve generalization in noisy-label MNIST training.

record.problems: The paper says it uses realistic but simple datasets with less attention to absolute performance. Many plotted results are not numerically reported in the text. The detailed phase example is a subset of MNIST with the mislabeled fraction not stated in the text; results on CIFAR10 are described as similar without corresponding numerical detail.

untested.parts: No matched comparison of natural-label generalization, near-perfect fitting of fully random labels, and chance held-out accuracy under random-label training.
No width sweep beyond the width needed for zero training error.
No convolutional versus fully connected test-error comparison or test of local connectivity.
No batch-size comparison under fixed epoch budgets or adapted recipes.
No magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness, generalization-gap ranking, or comparison against norm and margin measures. Gradient-noise spectra measure a different construct.
No removal based on inclusion-dependent own-label memorization, retraining comparison against equal-size random removal, or resulting accuracy penalty.

record.verdict_notes: T6 applies relative to the eight specified versions despite the study's own substantive generalization results. Qualitative results can establish effects; the cannot_determine states here reflect the absence of a matching claim version.

versions.untested_parts: Does not report fitting fixed random labels and comparing held-out performance with natural-label training under the same architecture and recipe.
No width sweep beyond the interpolation threshold.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison aimed at image generalization.
No adaptive optimizer versus SGD generalization comparison.
No magnitude-aware sharpness measurement or comparison of generalization gaps.
The cleaning method removes high-loss samples during mislabeled-data training; it does not identify and remove memorized examples by their effect on their own-label prediction.
